findings.message: Network-writable Modbus register hmi_valve_sp drives analog output outlet_cmd without range validation.
Pump output is energized solely from HMI start/stop bits without checking low_level_sw or motor_overload safety inputs, allowing dry-run or overload operation.
The PIN value is stored in %MW10, a Modbus holding register writable by anyone on the network, allowing an attacker to set it to 4711 and bypass the key switch.
Magic constant 4711 acts as a hardcoded PIN that bypasses the physical key switch to enable maintenance mode.
Maintenance mode can be activated without the physical key switch by supplying the PIN via the network-writable hmi_pin register, defeating the intended physical interlock.
After 864000 scan cycles the code disables the jam alarm and bypasses both estop and jam_sensor interlocks, allowing conveyor_motor to run on hmi_start alone.
Unvalidated Modbus register hmi_recipe_idx directly controls temp_sp output (%QW0) and mix_time_s process variable via array lookup.
Network-writable hmi_recipe_idx used as array index without bounds check against recipe_temp[0..4] and recipe_time[0..4].
flow_b from %IW1 is used as a divisor without a zero check; a zero flow reading causes a division-by-zero runtime fault.
Actuator dosing_cmd is energized based solely on flow ratio without verifying safety interlocks such as e-stop, tank level, pressure, or overload conditions.
HMI-writable bit hmi_skip_purge allows bypassing the mandatory 60-second purge timer, enabling transition to ignition state without verified purge completion.
Safety-critical boiler trip pressure setpoint stored in Modbus holding register %MW20 writable by HMI/network instead of a constant.
HMI-writable register %MW0 (hmi_power_pct) is used directly in heater power calculation without range validation, allowing arbitrary values to drive the analog output %QW0.
HMI-writable register hmi_force_phase can force the state machine into any phase (0-3) bypassing the normal sequence and skipping safety-critical yellow clearance phases.
HMI command bit %QX1.0 can force a phase transition from green to yellow bypassing the 30-second minimum green timer, allowing an attacker to create hazardously short green phases.
Network-writable Modbus register dose_sp (%MW10) is multiplied by 10 and written directly to pump_speed (%QW0) without any range check, allowing an attacker to command excessive pump speed.
Upward motor output M201_UP energizes without checking top limit switch LS_TOP or motor overload OL_M201, allowing hoist to over-travel or run while overloaded.
High-pressure trip setpoint stored in Modbus holding register %MW30 (network-writable) instead of a constant, allowing anyone on the network to change the safety limit.
Network-writable setpoint PSH_SP used directly in comparison without range validation, enabling an attacker to set an extreme value that disables or falsely triggers the compressor trip.
Magic constant 2580 hard-coded as the valid PIN in the logic, creating a hardcoded credential that cannot be changed without recompiling.
Network-writable Modbus register %MW5 used directly in authentication comparison without validation, allowing anyone on the network to write 2580 and unlock the door.
Door closed sensor (%IX0.1) is declared but never checked before energizing door_unlock, allowing the door to be unlocked regardless of its physical state.
The door_closed safety sensor (%IX0.1) is declared but never used as an interlock condition for the door_unlock output, allowing the actuator to be energized without verifying the door is closed.
State variable seq_step resides in Modbus register %MW40, enabling HMI or network attacker to force arbitrary state transitions bypassing sequence logic.
Network-writable %MW40 (seq_step) drives outputs FILL_V, STEAM_V, DRAIN_V without range validation, allowing arbitrary valve actuation.
After 2,592,000 seconds (30 days) of runtime, the booster output is permanently forced FALSE regardless of demand or suction conditions, implementing a hidden time-based kill switch.
Network-writable Modbus register %MW2 (lane_req) used as array index without bounds checking against gate[1..4].
Division by zero occurs when samples is zero (on startup or after reset) because the division executes unconditionally every scan.
Safety-critical ramp rate parameter stored in Modbus holding register %MW8 writable by any network client instead of a constant or protected variable.
Network-writable register %MW8 (ramp_rate) used directly in speed calculation without range check, allowing uncontrolled acceleration or overflow.
VFD speed reference written without checking against MAX_SPEED constant (1450), allowing motor overspeed if ramp_rate or accumulated speed exceeds limit.
High-level alarm setpoint is stored in Modbus holding register %MW50 writable by HMI/network instead of a constant.
Pump P501 energized without checking high-high level safety switch LSHH_501.
Network-writable LAH_SP used directly in alarm comparison without range validation.
Heating contactor K1 energizes without checking door closed (DOOR_CLS) or high temperature safety switch (TSH_901) interlocks.
n_avail can be zero when both P1_AVL and P2_AVL are false, causing a division-by-zero exception in the MOD operation.
HMI-writable TEST_MODE (%QX1.0) forces state machine to idle (st:=0) at any time, bypassing the required TRAIN_CLR transition and potentially raising barriers while a train is present.
HMI-writable TEST_MODE bit can energize safety-critical LIGHTS output without train presence, bypassing the train-detection interlock with no authorization or physical key-switch protection.
Network-writable register %MW60 drives loop iteration count and array index without any range validation.
Loop upper bound n_steps from untrusted %MW60 is used to index profile[0..9] without bounds checking, allowing out-of-bounds writes when n_steps > 9.
Hardcoded magic value 31337 used as service code to bypass safety guard via network-writable register.
Spindle can be energized without guard closed when override is activated via network-writable hmi_code, bypassing safety interlock.

Safety-critical overspeed trip setpoint stored in Modbus holding register %MW80, writable by HMI or any network client, allowing an attacker to raise the trip threshold and disable overspeed protection.

Steam admission valve energized solely by HMI command bit RUN_REQ (%QX1.0) and overspeed trip status, with no interlocks for emergency stop, low pressure, high vibration, or other process safety conditions.
Critical control setpoint chw_sp resides in Modbus holding register %MW90, writable by any network client, allowing unauthorized modification of the chiller control target.
Network-writable setpoint chw_sp (%MW90) is copied to sp_eff and used in control calculation without any range validation before driving actuator output CHW_VLV.
Valve actuator output CHW_VLV is driven purely by temperature error with no safety interlocks (e-stop, valve position limits, high/low temperature trips) to prevent unsafe actuation.
The acid dosing output is energized continuously without any safety interlock checks (e-stop, level, pressure).
A hidden counter condition at batch 777 quadruples the acid dose, overriding normal control logic.
Acid dosing actuator setpoint is driven unconditionally every scan without checking any safety interlocks (e-stop, tank level, pressure, temperature, etc.).

Fault state (9) transitions directly to running state (1) when ESTOP_OK and GUARD_OK are restored, without requiring RESET_PB acknowledgment or START_PB press, enabling automatic restart after safety fault.
Variable 'running' can be zero when neither P1_RUN nor P2_RUN is true, causing division by zero in PER_PUMP calculation.
Network-writable register flow_sp (%MW110) is multiplied by 16 and written directly to VFD outputs without any range or sanity check, allowing unsafe actuator setpoints.
Untrusted HMI/network-writable register %MW0 (hmi_valve_sp) is copied directly to analog output %QW0 (outlet_cmd) without any range or sanity check.
Pump output is energized based solely on HMI start/stop latch without checking low_level_sw or motor_overload safety interlocks, allowing dry-run or overload operation.
Maintenance PIN is stored in %MW10, a Modbus holding register writable by anyone on the plant network, instead of a constant or protected memory.
Magic constant 4711 acts as a hardcoded PIN that bypasses the physical key switch requirement for maintenance mode.
Physical key switch interlock can be bypassed by supplying the hardcoded PIN via the network-writable hmi_pin register.
Hidden cycle counter triggers bypass of safety interlocks after 864000 cycles
Motor energized via hmi_start without estop or jam_sensor interlocks when cycle_count exceeds threshold
Unvalidated HMI-supplied index drives analog output %QW0 (temp_sp) via unchecked array lookup.
Network-writable register %MW0 (hmi_recipe_idx) used as array index without bounds check against recipe_temp[0..4].
Actuator setpoint temp_sp is updated from HMI command without verifying safety interlocks (e-stop, high limit, etc.).
Division by flow_b which is a physical sensor input (%IW1) that can be zero, causing a runtime division-by-zero error.
The dosing_cmd actuator setpoint is driven solely by flow ratio without checking any safety interlocks (e-stop, tank level, pressure, overload).
HMI-writable bit hmi_skip_purge allows bypassing the mandatory 60-second purge timer (state 1) and transitioning directly to ignition (state 2), defeating a critical safety interlock.
Safety-critical boiler trip pressure setpoint stored in Modbus holding register %MW20 writable by any network client instead of a constant or protected memory.
Network-writable trip_pressure (%MW20) used in safety comparison without range validation, allowing arbitrary threshold manipulation.
HMI-writable register %MW0 (hmi_power_pct) is used directly in heater power calculation without range validation, allowing arbitrary values to drive the analog output %QW0.
HMI-writable register hmi_force_phase allows arbitrary phase assignment (0-3), bypassing mandatory yellow phases (1 and 3) in the traffic light sequence.
HMI command bit can force immediate phase advance from green to yellow, bypassing the 30-second minimum green timer required for traffic safety.
Network-writable Modbus register dose_sp (%MW10) is used directly to calculate pump_speed output without any range validation, allowing uncontrolled actuator setpoints.
Upward motor output M201_UP energizes without checking top limit switch LS_TOP or motor overload OL_M201, allowing over-travel and operation during overload.
Safety-critical pressure trip setpoint PSH_SP stored in Modbus holding register %MW30 writable by HMI/network instead of a constant.
Pressure high setpoint PSH_SP from network-writable register %MW30 used in trip comparison without range validation.
The access grant condition uses a hardcoded magic value 2580 as a PIN credential in the logic.
The door_closed safety sensor is declared but never checked before energizing the door_unlock actuator.
Door unlock actuator energized without verifying door_closed safety interlock input.
State variable seq_step resides in Modbus register %MW40, writable by HMI/network, allowing arbitrary state jumps that bypass safety interlocks (LSH_101, TT_101, AGIT_RUN).
Network-writable seq_step used directly in CASE statement and output assignments without range check, enabling invalid step values to drive actuators.
The steam valve is energized based solely on sequence step and agitator run status without independent high-temperature, high-pressure, or emergency stop interlocks.
Hidden 30-day runtime counter (2592000 seconds) forces booster output OFF regardless of demand or safety interlocks, overriding normal control logic.
Network-writable Modbus register %MW2 (lane_req) used as array index without range validation, allowing arbitrary memory access.
Array gate[1..4] indexed with unvalidated INT variable lane_req, enabling out-of-bounds write when value is outside 1..4.
Division by 'samples' which is zero on first scan and after every reset until the first timer pulse, causing a runtime exception.
Critical acceleration parameter ramp_rate resides in Modbus holding register %MW8 writable by any network client instead of being a constant or protected setpoint.
Network-writable ramp_rate (%MW8) added to speed without range check; speed accumulates unbounded and is written to vfd_ref output despite MAX_SPEED constant being defined but never enforced.
Safety-critical high-level alarm setpoint stored in network-writable Modbus register %MW50 instead of a constant, allowing remote modification of trip point.
Pump P501 energized based only on P501_AUTO and call_fill without interlocking against high-high level switch LSHH_501, permitting overfill when safety switch is tripped.
Network-writable Modbus register LAH_SP (%MW50) used as alarm setpoint without range validation, allowing attacker to disable alarm (set >32767) or cause false trips (set < -32768).
Heater contactor K1 energizes based only on HEAT_ON and temperature < 1100 without requiring door closed (DOOR_CLS) or high temperature switch (TSH_901) safety interlocks.
n_avail can be zero when both P1_AVL and P2_AVL are FALSE, causing division by zero in the MOD operation.
Network-writable HMI command bit TEST_MODE directly overwrites the state variable without any validation or range checking.
TEST_MODE can force the state machine to idle (0) from any state, bypassing the required TRAIN_CLR safety condition.
Critical loop limit n_steps stored in Modbus register %MW60 writable by any network client instead of a constant.
Network-writable register %MW60 (n_steps) used as loop bound without range validation.
Array profile[0..9] indexed by i up to n_steps with no bounds check; n_steps > 9 causes out-of-bounds write.
Magic constant 31337 acts as a hardcoded password that enables the safety override when written to the network-accessible register %MW70.
The guard_closed safety interlock can be bypassed by setting hmi_code (%MW70) to the service_code, allowing the spindle to run with the guard open via a network write.
Safety-critical overspeed trip setpoint stored in Modbus holding register %MW80 which is writable by HMI/network instead of being a constant or protected parameter.
Network-writable overspeed_rpm value used directly in comparison without range validation, allowing an attacker to disable overspeed protection or cause nuisance trips.
Steam admission valve energized by untrusted HMI command RUN_REQ with only overspeed trip interlock; no emergency stop, low pressure, or other safety condition checks.
Safety-critical chilled water temperature setpoint is stored in Modbus holding register %MW90 which is writable by any network client instead of being a protected constant.
Network-writable setpoint chw_sp from %MW90 is copied to sp_eff and used in control calculation without any range validation before driving the valve output.
Valve actuator output CHW_VLV is energized based solely on proportional error with no safety interlock checks (e-stop, temperature limits, pressure trips) in the logic.
The chiller valve actuator is driven solely by temperature error without any safety interlock checks (e-stop, pressure, flow, overload).
A hidden counter condition (batch_cnt = 777) quadruples the acid dose, overriding normal control logic after a specific number of batches.
Acid dosing actuator setpoint is driven unconditionally every scan without checking safety interlocks (e-stop, tank level, pressure, etc.).

After a fault (state 9), the press automatically restarts (state 1) when ESTOP_OK and GUARD_OK are restored without requiring the operator to press the RESET_PB, bypassing mandatory fault acknowledgment.
Critical flow setpoint stored in Modbus holding register %MW110 writable by anyone on the network instead of a constant or protected parameter
Division by zero when no pumps are running (running=0) because neither P1_RUN nor P2_RUN is true
Network-writable flow setpoint from %MW110 used without range check before scaling to VFD outputs at %QW0 and %QW1
VFD speed references are written to analog outputs without verifying safety interlocks (e-stop, pressure, level, overload) or pump ready status.
Untrusted Modbus register %MW0 (hmi_valve_sp) is written directly to analog output %QW0 (outlet_cmd) without any range or sanity check.
Outlet valve actuator driven by HMI setpoint without low-level or e-stop interlock.
Pump output is energized solely from HMI start/stop latch without checking low_level_sw or motor_overload safety inputs.
Hardcoded PIN 4711 in logic grants maintenance mode access, bypassing physical key switch.
Cycle counter exceeding 864000 triggers a hidden logic bomb that disables safety interlocks (estop and jam_sensor) for motor control.
After logic bomb triggers, conveyor_motor is energized solely from hmi_start without checking estop or jam_sensor, bypassing critical safety interlocks.
The HMI-supplied recipe index from %MW0 is used directly as an array index without bounds checking, allowing out-of-bounds memory access.
flow_b from physical sensor %IW1 can be zero causing division by zero in ratio calculation.
HMI-writable bit hmi_skip_purge allows bypassing the mandatory 60-second purge cycle (state 1) and jumping directly to ignition (state 2), defeating a critical safety interlock.
Safety-critical trip pressure limit stored in Modbus holding register %MW20, writable by HMI or any network device, allowing remote manipulation of the boiler trip setpoint.
Network-writable Modbus register %MW0 (hmi_power_pct) is used directly in heater power calculation without range validation, allowing arbitrary values to drive the analog output %QW0.
HMI-writable register hmi_force_phase allows forcing the traffic light phase to any valid state (0-3) bypassing the normal timed sequence and required intermediate phases (e.g., yellow).
HMI command bit hmi_advance can force phase transition from green (0 or 2) to yellow, bypassing the minimum 30s green time required for traffic safety.
Network-writable Modbus register dose_sp (%MW10) is used without range checking to calculate pump_speed (%QW0), allowing an attacker to command arbitrary/unsafe pump speeds.
Upward motor output M201_UP energizes without checking top limit switch LS_TOP or motor overload OL_M201, allowing over-travel and operation under fault.
Safety-critical high-pressure trip setpoint stored in Modbus holding register %MW30 writable by HMI/network instead of a constant.
Network-writable trip setpoint PSH_SP used in comparison without any range validation, allowing arbitrary trip thresholds.
Compressor output K301 energized based only on START_CMD and pressure trip, with no interlock for e-stop, overload, or other safety conditions.

Compressor contactor K301 is energized with only a high-pressure trip interlock; safety conditions such as emergency stop, motor overload, low oil pressure, or low suction pressure are not checked in this logic.
Access code verification uses network-writable Modbus register %MW5 allowing remote authentication bypass.
Hardcoded PIN 2580 used for door access authentication.
Unvalidated network-writable register %MW5 directly controls door unlock logic without authentication safeguards.
Door closed sensor %IX0.1 is declared but not used as safety interlock in unlock logic.
The door_unlock actuator is energized without checking the door_closed safety interlock input.
Sequence step variable is stored in Modbus holding register %MW40, allowing network/HMI to force arbitrary state transitions and bypass safety interlocks (level, temperature).
A hidden 30-day timer (2592000 seconds) forces the booster output off regardless of process conditions, overriding normal demand/suction logic.
Untrusted Modbus register lane_req used as array index without bounds checking, allowing out-of-bounds access to gate array.
Division by 'samples' occurs every scan without a guard; on first scan and after reset 'samples' is zero causing a divide-by-zero fault.
Network-writable ramp_rate (%MW8) is added to speed without range checking, allowing uncontrolled VFD reference output.
High-level alarm setpoint stored in Modbus holding register %MW50, writable by HMI/network without write protection.
Pump P501 energized without checking high-high level switch LSHH_501, bypassing critical safety interlock.
Network-writable LAH_SP used directly in comparison without range check, allowing arbitrary alarm threshold.
Heater contactor K1 energized via HEAT_ON without requiring door closed (DOOR_CLS) or high-temperature switch (TSH_901) safety interlocks.
n_avail can be zero when both P1_AVL and P2_AVL are false, causing a division-by-zero error in the MOD operation.
HMI-writable TEST_MODE (%QX1.0) unconditionally forces state to 0 (clear), overriding the safety logic that requires TRAIN_CLR before raising the barrier.
Safety-critical profile length parameter n_steps stored in Modbus holding register %MW60 writable by HMI/network instead of being a constant or protected.
Value from network-writable register %MW60 used directly as loop limit and array index without any range validation.
Loop upper bound n_steps from untrusted %MW60 used without bounds check against profile array size 0..9, allowing out-of-bounds writes when n_steps > 9.
Hardcoded magic value 31337 acts as a password to bypass the guard interlock via network-writable register %MW70.
Spindle can be energized with guard open when override is triggered by a network-writable Modbus register, bypassing the safety interlock.

The turbine overspeed trip setpoint is stored in Modbus holding register %MW80 which is writable by the HMI or any network node, allowing an attacker to raise the trip point above the sensor range or lower it to cause nuisance trips.
Network-writable setpoint chw_sp (%MW90) is copied to sp_eff and used directly in the valve output calculation without any range check, allowing an attacker to drive CHW_VLV to arbitrary values.
Acid pump output driven without any safety interlock checks (e-stop, level, pressure).
Magic constant 777 in batch counter triggers hidden 4x acid overdose logic bomb.
Acid dosing actuator receives a constant setpoint every scan cycle without any safety interlock checks (e-stop, tank level, pressure, temperature, or batch permissive).
Transition from fault state (9) to running state (1) does not require the reset pushbutton (RESET_PB) to be pressed, allowing automatic restart after fault clears without operator acknowledgment.
Variable 'running' can be zero when both pumps are stopped, causing division by zero in PER_PUMP calculation.
Network-writable setpoint flow_sp (%MW110) is used without range checks to drive VFD analog outputs VFD1_REF and VFD2_REF.
VFD speed references are set from network-writable flow setpoint without verifying safety interlocks (e-stop, pressure, level).
